series_label: Maternal mortality ratio (modeled estimate, per 100,000 live births)
source_or_custodian: World Development Indicators (WB_WDI); estimates by the Maternal Mortality Estimation Inter-Agency Group (WHO, UNICEF, UNFPA, World Bank Group, and UNDESA/Population Division)
status_or_notes: The server has no data for 2024 or 2025 (latest year is 2023), so only 2000-2023 are returned. No uncertainty intervals were returned. Limitation noted by the server: the methodology differs from that used for previous estimates, so data should not be compared historically; ratios are of unknown reliability and cannot be assumed to be exact. The SDG indicator 3.1.1 note is also given.
definition: Maternal mortality ratio is the number of women who die from pregnancy-related causes while pregnant or within 42 days of pregnancy termination per 100,000 live births. The data are estimated with a regression model using information on the proportion of maternal deaths among non-AIDS deaths in women ages 15-49, fertility, birth attendants, and GDP measured using purchasing power parities (PPPs).
